title.narrative: Establishing Women and Children Service Centers

description.narrative: The objective of the JFPR is to reduce vulnerability and helplessness of women and children in 5 rural districts of Nepal by providing professional and coordinated protection and assistance to female and child victims of crimes such as rape, domestic violence, polygamy, allegations of witchcraft, child abuse, child marriage and trafficking. This will increase their chances of reintegration into mainstream society and thus their participation in the development process eventually leading to poverty reduction.
Improved access by Nepalese women and children in 20 rural districts of Nepal to legal protection and social support services.

50% increase in confidence in WCSCs and supporting agencies by the end of the project. Progress/Status: Confidence of people to go to police is 64% (End Line Survey Report 2018) Data Source: - Police crime reports at district level - Public opinion surveys - Victim surveys - Progress reports from the executing agency - Reports from ADB TA review missions Actual value:

At least 60% of crimes against women and children reported in the last 2 years of the project are satisfactorily handled by WCSCs and the supporting agencies. Progress/Status: 65% of crimes against Women and children reported in the end of the project are satisfactorily handled by WCSCs and the supporting agencies (End line Survey Report 2018) Data Source: - Police crime reports at district level - Public opinion surveys - Victim surveys - Progress reports from the executing agency - Reports from ADB TA review missions Actual value:

Increase of 30% in the number of reported crimes against women and children in the first 2 years of implementation (from 2009 baseline). Progress/Status: Increase of 36% in the number of reported crimes against women and children in the first 2 years of implementation. Data Source: - Police crime reports at district level - Public opinion surveys - Victim surveys - Progress reports from the executing agency - Reports from ADB TA review missions Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Civil society consultations and awareness-raising undertaken in WCSC districts. Indicator: a. One information campaign through media outlets carried out in the first 6 months of project implementation. Progress/Status: - Information campaign through local Radio FM was carried out continuously in 15 districts.
- Monitoring was carried out by local police station on effects of the message broadcasted from local radio FMs. Audio drama on cybercrimes in Nepali, Maithili and Awadhi language has been broadcasted. It is found that there is maximum access to information about GBV, legal provisions and reporting procedures in the communities. In addition, the number of reporting of cases against GBV has increased.
- 7 PSA on cybercrimes, domestic violence and human trafficking, dowry, child marriage, rape and child labor were telecast from 7 TV channels. 3 short video clips on cybercrimes, domestic violence and human trafficking, drama type 4 long videos has been disseminated at community level.
- Awareness raising campaign (through interaction, video show, street drama, and student sensitization) was carried out in 871 communities of 456 VDC/Gaunpalikas and 71 Municipalities. Many success stories came up at the community level after awareness program. Orientation was provided to district Police team (WCSC/DPO/APO/PS) on details of project and updating and reporting of crimes/violence data as required to project. Altogether, 583 (82 women) police personnel were oriented on project. Staffs were familiar on implementation methodology, update records and report to PIU. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 1. Civil society consultations and awareness-raising undertaken in WCSC districts. Indicator: b. Three workshops carried out in each districts, with outcome reports - by month 6. Progress/Status: - Three civil society consultation workshops were carried out in each of 15 districts (45 workshops) and inputs collected. Altogether 3185 persons (1479 women) participated. Among them, 629 were police personnel. The roles and responsibilities of civil societies, government stakeholders and political parties were identified for collective action to prevent crimes/violence in their areas. Collective actions were carried out by stakeholders with DPO/WCSC as they expressed their commitments during the workshop. District level GBV control network committee has been formed during the workshop. An increment was found in the collaboration among the stakeholders after the consultation workshop in each district. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 1. Civil society consultations and awareness-raising undertaken in WCSC districts. Indicator: c. One survey in the project districts in years 1 and 3 with analystical reports on their results. Progress/Status: - Baseline survey completed for all 20 districts. Report has been shared with stakeholders.
- One survey against DMF (2017) and one survey regarding GBV control network (2018) conducted. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 1. Civil society consultations and awareness-raising undertaken in WCSC districts. Indicator: d. One strategy paper for each new WCSC developed - by month 6. Progress/Status: - Strategy paper for each WCSC has been developed, printed and orientation provided to 20 project districts (including pilot districts) for its implementation. It is being implemented by WCSCs but not properly followed the developed strategy paper. Strategic Plan of each 15 districts has been developed by revising strategy paper considering the federal structure of local government and NP.
- Based on lessons learned from project one WCSC strategy has been developed for all 77 districts, it has been printed, will be dispatched to all districts for its implementation. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 2. Central WCSC in Kathmandu and 20 district WCSCs established. Indicator: a. One central WCSC operational in Kathmandu - within year 1. Progress/Status: Functional office is in operation in NPHQ with new building completed. Furthermore, the crimes/violence data against women and children of 77 districts were updated and analyzed and shared with stakeholders. Besides, there is continuous working for prevention, control and investigation of violence against women and children and coordinating with stakeholders in order to provide support services to survivors. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 2. Central WCSC in Kathmandu and 20 district WCSCs established. Indicator: b. The 20 target districts have an operational WCSC and network of supporting agencies by 2017. Progress/Status: 19 districts WCSCs, including 5 pilot districts, are in operation with minimum 3 and maximum 5 staffs who are working and are able to handle the reported cases and report to WCSD/PIU, regional and Zonal police office. Moreover, the awareness raising program with network members at community level is being implemented. 19 districts WCSCs have own functional buildings. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 3. Institutional capacity of the Nepal Police in dealing with crimes against women and children strengthened. Indicator: 30 police trainers trained in the new training programs (data disaggregated by sex). Progress/Status: - 45 senior police officers (2 women) were trained on gender responsive investigation and counselling skills including gender disaggregated data.
- Trainers have been mobilized in 15 district level training for local level police personnel and network members. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 3. Institutional capacity of the Nepal Police in dealing with crimes against women and children strengthened. Indicator: 900 police and service providers representatives trained in gender-based violence and communication skills (data disaggregated by sex). Progress/Status: - 1021 police personnel and service providers' representatives were trained. Among them, 450 police personnel (189 women) were trained on gender responsive investigation and counseling skills including communication skills and, gender disaggregated data collection.
- 571 (423 women) members of district and VDC level GBV network Committee were trained on capacity enhancement.
- Rapid training need assessment (TNA) has been undertaken by project through HRD Specialist and designed the training modules based on the findings of TNA.
- New 4 days training on Capacity building training for 449 participants (373 Female) to VDC/Municipality level GBV control network members in Dhading, Rasuwa, Dolakha, Tanahun,Gorkha, Siraha, Saptari, Mahottari, Sindhuli, Rolpa, Pyuthan, Doti, Jumla district has been conducted.
- 10 days psychosocial support training to police personnel from 20 project districts in 2 slots for 50 participants (17 women) and 4 days capacity building training in 2 slots for the same 50 participants has been provided. Apart from this, a 3 days psychosocial support training to 22 members ( 14 women) of district level GBV control network members and 3 days capacity building training to 60 members (47 women) for district level GBV control network members has been provided through ADB TA.
- A 3 days online GBV database administration system has been provided to 9 WCSD staff ( 6 women). Likewise, 3 days training on online GBV database system was conducted for 20 WCSC staff ( 10 women) from project districts. And one day training on GBV database administration system was provided to 4 technical staff of Crime Investigation Department. Operational Manual on online GBV database system have been developed for WCSC staff.
- 14 days proposal and report writing training provided to 6 Senior Police Officers ( 4 women) of WCSD. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 3. Institutional capacity of the Nepal Police in dealing with crimes against women and children strengthened. Indicator: At least 3 women staff, including at least one woman police officer, trained and deployed to each WCSC. Progress/Status: - 56 woman staff including 7 senior officers and 9 woman junior officers are deployed in 20 WCSCs (2 to 7 woman staff in each WCSC ); - 7 senior officers and 9 woman junior officers are deployed in 8 WCSCs - 189 woman staff of 15 districts were trained on gender responsive investigation and counseling skills. - 17 WCSC woman staff have been trained on psycho social counseling supporter training and capacity development training. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 3. Institutional capacity of the Nepal Police in dealing with crimes against women and children strengthened. Indicator: Seven training modules on investigation and handling of crimes against women and children, and on counseling, integrated into police training by 2014. Progress/Status: - Seven training modules on (1) concept of Gender and Gender Based Violence (GBV), (2) Legal treatment related to GBV, (3) Gender Responsive Investigation Procedure, (4) Practical exercise on investigation process of violence/crime cases, (5) Analysis impact of sexual assault on boys and girls, (6)Communication and behaviour with women and child victims and (7) psychosocial counselling etc, have been integrated in different related training curriculum of Nepal Police.
- 10 days psychosocial supporter training curriculum incorporated in the annual training calendar of Nepal Police. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 4. Coordination between district WCSCs and other services strengthened. Indicator: a. Twenty districts have a network that has met at least 20 times in the previous year, by 2017. Progress/Status: 20 districts have functional networks. 15 districts and 44 local level network committees were formed in 15 new project districts. Per end line survey 2018, 16 districts had at least 10 meetings in FY 2016/17; the districts not having at least 10 meetings were: Saptari and Rautahat which had 6 meetings each and Tanahun and Pyuthan which had 9 meetings each. Data Source: - Police reports - Progress reports from the executing agency - Minutes of focus groups and network meetings - Minutes of communities meetings - Public opinion survey reports - Aide memoire from ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: 2. Central WCSC in Kathmandu and 20 district WCSCs established. Indicator: c. WCSCs provided with basic office package (computer, printer, camera, tape recorder, basic office furnishing and accessories). Progress/Status: - Basic office package (laptop, projector, printer (three in one), camera, desktop computer, voice recorder, generator, sound box) were procured and delivered to WCSCs.
- A four wheeler vehicle for central WCSC, 6 motorbikes and 7 scooters were procured for district WCSCs. The motorbikes and scooters have been handed over to the 13 districts.
- Two four wheeler vehicles for Bajhang and Achham and 5 motorbikes for center and districts were procured and on use.
Furnishing of central WCSC and 15 WCSCs completed.
